> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 69 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1687bd864c19d9bf10138e847ae65b0700c1ab1c` — the merge of head `c797375ab28ac06e9a966064b6a5e3986a016572` into base `e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1687bd864c19d9bf10138e847ae65b0700c1ab1c && git checkout 1687bd864c19d9bf10138e847ae65b0700c1ab1c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce c797375ab28ac06e9a966064b6a5e3986a016572 && git checkout -B drift-repro e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce && git merge --no-ff c797375ab28ac06e9a966064b6a5e3986a016572

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e7344f0a1ba41b97947e7738c358d35c570fb4ce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c797375ab28ac06e9a966064b6a5e3986a016572`

<sub>Read: card #20157 body + 3 comments, #19995 body + ruling C (5852158605) + engine decision 5823452098, #20158 body, PR #20213 object/body/7-file list/6 commits/full diff (626+/3-) and check-runs; at the head: `objectql-engine.ts` (member, two types, header amendment, top-docblock evidence bar), `engine.ts` (`lowerWhereFilterArray`, `resolveWhereFilterTokens`, `admissionRefusalOf`, `judgeWhereAdmission`, `judgeFilter`, `resolveObjectName`, `mergeReadContext`, `foldEngineOptionAliases`, `requireFindOnePredicate`, `expandSearchOnAst`, and the six verbs' where paths), the door modules' throw sites (objectql `filter-comparand-shape.ts`, text and temporal doors; spec shape/type faces, `parseFilterAST`; core `filter-tokens.ts`), `read-scope-sql.ts` (#5367 text, `assertReadScopePlaceholdersResolvable`), `objectql-strategy.ts` merge site, the changeset, both generated JSONs, both test files, the two changeset gates' headers. Ran, in a detached worktree at the head with frozen install and the objectql dependency closure restored from turbo cache (exit 0): the PR's `engine-judge-filter.test.ts` (43/43), and a review probe of 17 filter cases x 6 verbs (102 pairs) at the head and again with `engine.ts` swapped to the branch base `d7c024133`, comparing execution fields byte for byte. NOT MEASURED: the full objectql/spec/consumer suites and every gate family (CI's, read from the check-runs), the spec type pins under `tsc` (CI type-check covers them), the merge ref locally (CI's), the HTTP leg of either consumer.</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

(a) Execution byte-identical: yes. The `engine.ts` diff is +127/-2; the only two removed lines are the two spellings `resolveFilterTokens(x, filterTokenContextFrom(ctx))` in `resolveWhereTokens` and `withResolvedWhere`, replaced by `resolveWhereFilterTokens(x, ctx)` whose body is exactly that expression (same call, same context builder, same return by reference). Every other hunk is an addition (one type import, three module functions, one method). No verb call site moved. Probe: 102 verb x case pairs (85 refusals) on base and head; `ok / code / status / message / driver calls / driver-seen where` identical, sha256 `c3732e8e…` on both sides; the door cases include the five card classes plus list-shape, comparand-type, non-object where, bad array sugar, non-filter array, unresolved placeholder, two-defect order, and an unregistered object. All six verbs refused at the door with zero driver calls on both sides.

(b) Same stages, same order, nothing else: yes. `judgeWhereAdmission` calls `lowerWhereFilterArray(object, operation, { where }, schema)` then `resolveWhereFilterTokens(admitted.where, context)` and nothing else; those are the two functions every verb calls (`engine.ts` 11203/11281, 11499/11553, 12943/12956, 15581/15585, 16098/16114, 16202/16410). `judgeFilter` resolves the object through the same `resolveObjectName` and reads the same `_registry.getObject(object)` as the verbs. Spy pins are real: the recording driver wraps every method into `calls`; `getDriver` is `vi.spyOn`'d on the instance (a judge calling `this.getDriver` would trip it, and any driver method call would land in `calls` regardless of route); hook and middleware are `vi.fn`; each assertion has a positive control on execution. Probe: judge driver calls 0 on all 102 pairs.

(c) Divergence risk: every `where` door in `engine.ts` sits inside `lowerWhereFilterArray` (962–1086); the door calls at 16254–16303 and 16369–16371 are the per-aggregation `filter` and `having` slots, not `where`. What execution runs around the stages and the judge does not: `foldEngineOptionAliases` / `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` (option keys; a caller passing `where` is unaffected), `getDriver` (before stage 1 on update/delete, between the stages on the reads), `assertWriteAllowed` / `enforceTransactionOrigin` on the writes, `expandSearchOnAst` on find/findOne (composes an engine-built `search` filter into `where`; `search` is outside the judge's input), and `requireFindOnePredicate` on findOne (probe: `where: []` on findOne refused at execution by a bare `Error` with no `code`/`status`, judge ok). The docblock names the first three families and not the last two; both are selectivity/option guards rather than runnability doors, the findOne guard has no ADR-0112 envelope so it could never be a returned verdict, and neither consumer meets them (#19995 runs `aggregate`; #20158 judges a policy filter whose emptiness its own `assertReadScopeCannotVacate` refuses first). Below admission (security middleware composition, hooks, driver-sql's `{ $field }` referent and `addDays` rule) is stated in the member docblock, the changeset and the Acceptance notes. On the reads, stage 2 runs on `mergeReadContext(query.context, options.context)`; the judge takes `context` directly, and the docblock says "the execution context the filter would run with". Main since the branch base: `e5cf27d65` edits `engine.ts` 16242–16410 (having/per-aggregation, disjoint from this PR's hunks), `4db1bf171` deletes elsewhere in the two generated JSONs, `e7f69dbba` adds a `{record_id}` refusal inside the shared core resolver, `e7344f0a1` adds an `$ne` array refusal inside the shared spec shape face; no seam signature changed, so both new refusals are judged automatically; `mergeable: true`, CI on the merge ref green. Safe for both consumers.

(d) Placeholders: `resolveFilterTokens` throws `UnknownFilterTokenError` (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400) or `UnresolvedFilterTokenError` (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED` / 400); `resolveFilterToken` returns `ctx.userId` / `ctx.orgId` only when truthy and throws otherwise, so a placeholder never resolves to `null`. The judge feeds `options.context` through the same `filterTokenContextFrom`. #19995's consumer already calls `assertReadScopePlaceholdersResolvable(scope, objectName, ctx.context)` = `resolveFilterTokens(scope, filterTokenContextFrom(context))`, so the judge's answer is the answer that consumer already computes. Probe: unresolved placeholder agrees on all six verbs; with `{ userId: 'u_1' }` the judge is ok and the driver saw `{ owner_id: 'u_1' }`. Pinned in the PR's test (two cases) and in the `EngineFilterJudgementOptions.context` docblock.

(e) #5367: the judge's `message` is the door's own text and names fields and comparands (probe: `'amount'`, `'closes_on'`, `{bogus_token}`, the `$in` value). The contract says so three times, honestly: `EngineFilterJudgement` ("the refusing door's own text, so it names fields, operators and comparands"), the member docblock ("The verdict is not redacted … a read-scope policy, the #5367 ruling … withholds the message itself"), and the changeset. That split is the one the engine decision 5823452098 ordered (doors keep their diagnostics for CRUD callers; the analytics face withholds) and matches `read-scope-sql.ts` (`READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` / 500, message to the operator's log only). No leak is introduced by this PR: no consumer is wired.

(f) Header amendment: the base header says members beyond `IDataEngine` are REQUIRED and why; the PR adds one three-line paragraph naming `judgeFilter` as the single exception by ruling and the reason (callers must work with an engine that lacks it). The top-docblock evidence bar ("declared only where a cross-package consumer already calls it") is untouched; the member is declared ahead of its call sites by ruling and its own docblock says so. Correct and minimal. The spec test pins optional, synchronous, the exact six-verb union, and the exact refusal keys.

(g) Surface: `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly the two type entries (`EngineFilterJudgement` type, `EngineFilterJudgementOptions` interface), regenerated; `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` are inside the green "Lint & Repo Gates". `packages/objectql` `package.json`, `index.ts`, `core.ts` are not in the file list, so its accept set is unchanged; the method is reached through the `IObjectQLEngine` instance.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes` on its own line in the body and in the changeset. Changeset: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: minor`. Against `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s stated rules: no `major` (launch-window guard), and the level axis requires a clause-② PR to grade at least one package whose published source it moves `minor` or above (both are, and both have published source in the diff); `check-empty-changeset.mjs`: the frontmatter is non-empty and no foreign changeset is modified. A new optional interface member, two new type exports and a new public engine method are additive, so `minor` is the correct level for both packages, not `patch`. "Check Changeset" = success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags
Blocking: none
Non-blocking: (1) the dev's open question for #20158 (a `classify` placeholder mode): option A is what execution answers and what #19995's consumer already computes; B would widen a just-published contract with no call site; left for #20158's own dispatch. (2) The out-of-scope note (`{ $field }` referent and `addDays` rule enforced only by driver-sql on `where`): below the judge's stated boundary, all five card classes are inside it; a landed measurement, not this PR's. (3) Acceptance-note claim that the eleven withheld classes are stage-1 doors: confirmed by reading (`assertReadScopeComparandsRunnable` calls `assertListComparandShapes` and `normalizeFilterComparandTypes`, both inside `lowerWhereFilterArray`) and by the probe's list-shape and comparand-type cases on six verbs. (4) Body inaccuracy: "behind origin/main by commits that touch none of these files" is false (`e5cf27d65` touches `engine.ts`, `4db1bf171` the two generated JSONs); the hunks are disjoint, the PR is mergeable and CI on the merge ref is green. (5) Docblock omission: `requireFindOnePredicate` (findOne) and `expandSearchOnAst` (find/findOne) run between the stages and are not in the "what differs by verb" list; neither is a `where` runnability door, and neither reaches a consumer. (6) The consumer suites were run by the dev at `30dadfba7`, one docblock commit before the head; CI at the head covers them.

CI at this head: 35 check-runs on `c797375ab28ac06e9a966064b6a5e3986a016572`, converged: 32 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 0 failed, 0 in progress. Green: Build Core, Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (6/6 shards + rollup), Type Check (source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, workspace, TypeScript Type Check), Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3 + rollup), Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the four PR-claim guards, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, filter. Closing keywords: the body carries exactly `Fixes #20157` and no other closing keyword.
